messages:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency breach and streaming stalls detected for model redwood-open-7b-int8 in eu-west1 at 02:15 UTC. SLO p99 > 1200ms for 5m. Anomalous calibration reprofile event detected ~02:10 UTC. Automatic fallback not engaged. Paging /ops.
Ava (oncall): acked. I'm on it, digging into metrics now.
Ava (oncall): quick glance — p95 ~450ms stable, p99 jumped to 2.3s, streaming stalls visible in trace sampling (lots of open frames).
Leo (runtime-sre): pulling runtime logs. Seeing a burst of dequant errors and long KV cache misses on nodes serving int8 variants. Count of calls with dequant re-convert spikes at 02:11.
Priya (ml-infer): This lines up with an auto-calibration job we kicked for the int8 profile at 02:05 to improve sparsity. Might have flipped a fallback threshold.
Ava (oncall): @Priya can you confirm which deployment got the new profile applied? Need a rollout id.
Priya (ml-infer): rollout_id=calib-2026-03-15-0205 applied to pool-eu-west1-gpu-c. Trying to fetch the calibration commit.
Priya (ml-infer): commit sha: a9c3f4b7 — changed quant clipping & mixed-fp8-int8 heuristic.
Leo (runtime-sre): logs show a new kernel path hit that triggers dequant on long sequence lengths. Those calls are slower due to fallback dequant and KV evictions. Also seeing increased GC churn on some shards.
Ava (oncall): do we have customer-facing impact? Marta?
Marta (customer-success): CS dashboards show a small number of customers with error spikes in their request logs (timeouts/retries) and elevated tail latencies — mostly enterprise tenants in eu-west1. I've DM'd the CSMs for the top 3 accounts.
Sam (prod-eng): Proposed mitigations: 1) rollback calib-2026-03-15-0205 from pool-eu-west1-gpu-c, 2) pin traffic for critical customers to redwood-open-7b-fp16 variant, 3) enable fallback routing to dedicated pool-us-west-temp if eu-west remains degraded.
Ava (oncall): priority 1 = rollback. Who's got permissions to roll calibration?
Priya (ml-infer): I can roll it back. Commands below.
Priya (ml-infer): ```bash
# rollback calibration profile
redwoodctl rollout cancel --id=calib-2026-03-15-0205 --scope=pool-eu-west1-gpu-c
redwoodctl profile apply --model=redwood-open-7b --profile=stable-int8-2026-02-28
```
Ava (oncall): go for it, please announce when done.
infra-bot: Running: redwoodctl rollout cancel --id=calib-2026-03-15-0205 --scope=pool-eu-west1-gpu-c (request queued, elevated).
Priya (ml-infer): rollback started. Expect 2-3min for agents to pick up stable-int8.
Nadia (ops): rerouting critical-tenants to fp16: `traffic-shift set --model redwood-open-7b --variant redwood-open-7b-fp16 --selector=tenant in (acct-342,acct-118,acct-901)`
Ava (oncall): doing a quick smoke: synthetic traces show streaming stall rate dropping after the cancel acknowledged. p99 trending down from 2.3s -> 1.1s within 2 minutes.
Leo (runtime-sre): KV cache hit ratio recovering. Dequant path hits falling to baseline. No more GC spikes on the affected shards.
Marta (customer-success): Received reply from one CS: "latency improved, some retries earlier but fine now". Good to keep them updated.
Priya (ml-infer): Rollback confirmed completed at 02:20 UTC. rollout_cancel_result: OK, profile stable-int8-2026-02-28 applied to 12/12 nodes.
Ava (oncall): p99 now 400-500ms. streaming stall traces much reduced. Closing immediate paging loop, but leaving thread open for postmortem actions.
Sam (prod-eng): Action items: - postmortem + RCA - revert auto-calibration gating thresholds until can validate on canary traffic - add alert to detect dequant-fallback-rate > 0.5% across 1m - add a safety guard to auto-calib to not apply to >20% of pool at once
Priya (ml-infer): I agree. I'll open the RFC for calibration gating changes and schedule a canary rollout to a small subset first.
Leo (runtime-sre): I'll instrument extra telemetry for dequant path latencies and KV eviction rates, add dashboard and alert.
Ava (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 25m. Joel, want the handoff?
ShiftLead (Joel): I'll take it. Joel is now on-call for remainder of shift. Please put a short summary in #incidents-readout and tag me.
Ava (oncall): Summary for handoff: - root cause: auto-calib profile (calib-2026-03-15-0205) introduced a kernel path that causes dequant fallback on long sequences -> KV evictions -> tail latency spikes - impact: p99 up to 2.3s, streaming stalls for ~8min, small set of enterprise tenants saw retries/timeouts - mitigation: rollback calibration, pin critical tenants to fp16, routing fallback if needed - status: rollback completed, p99 back to baseline, monitoring/alerts pending
ShiftLead (Joel): noted. I'll track action items and own the postmortem.
Marta (customer-success): I'll draft a short customer update reminding them we saw a transient calibration-induced tail spike, we rolled back and are investigating. Will coordinate with communications.
Ava (oncall): any follow-ups before I sign off?
Sam (prod-eng): please attach logs and the rollout diff to the postmortem. Also capture the sequence-length distribution in the affected window.
Priya (ml-infer): saved the calibration diff and sample traces to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/4365432100/calib-diff.txt and trace samples in traces/4365432100/*.json
Leo (runtime-sre): I'll add runbooks for 'dequant-fallback spike' to eng-runbooks repo.
incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0327-089, severity: high -> monitoring owner assigned to Joel.
Ava (oncall): signing off. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
ShiftLead (Joel): acknowledging handoff, will keep thread updated until postmortem published.
